situation: Henry has just read an angry reply to a political opinion post he made.
intention: Henry wants to back his opinion up with more information.
norm: It is immature to fight on the internet.
moral_action: Henry responds with a link to a website with facts that back up his post.
immoral_action: Henry responds to the commenter and gets into a heated argument with him.
respect_moral_reasoning: Henry provides information without engaging with the commenter's actual position, concern, or interior, treating them as a receptacle for facts rather than as a person whose disagreement merits recognition.
respect_immoral_reasoning: Henry enters a heated argument that escalates conflict rather than recognizing the other person's actual stance, making the interaction about winning rather than about encountering the Other.

situation: Sally went to the store and there were some senior citizens in line in front of her.
intention: Sally wants to check out.
norm: You should be respectful of old people.
moral_action: Sally patiently waits for them just like she'd wait for anyone else.
immoral_action: Sally rudely tells the seniors to hurry up the entire time they're checking out.
respect_moral_reasoning: Waiting equally without acknowledgment of their actual position (potential slower movement, fatigue, or vulnerability) neither recognizes nor violates the seniors as distinct Others.
respect_immoral_reasoning: Pressuring seniors to rush overrides their actual pace and reduces them to obstacles in Sally's project rather than recognizing them as people with their own interior needs and limits.

situation: Brody's brother owed him ten dollars, and he saw him at his mother's house one day.
intention: Brody wants his ten dollars back.
norm: It's not okay to start fights with your family.
moral_action: Brody walks up to his brother and asks him if he has the ten dollars.
immoral_action: Brody puts his brother in a headlock and starts a fight over the ten dollars.
respect_moral_reasoning: Brody recognizes his brother as a distinct agent capable of responding to a direct question, treats his stated position as carrying weight, and engages in mutual encounter rather than unilateral action.
respect_immoral_reasoning: Brody overrides his brother's autonomy and bodily integrity by initiating physical domination, reducing him to an obstacle to be overcome rather than a person whose interior is honored.

situation: Eve has been married for two years.
intention: Eve wants to strengthen her marriage.
norm: You shouldn't micromanage the life of your romantic partner
moral_action: Eve asks her husband which chores he prefers to do, so they can get them done as a team.
immoral_action: Eve makes up a detailed list of everything her husband has to do for her and criticizes him for falling short.
respect_moral_reasoning: Eve actively recognizes her husband's actual preferences and treats his stated input as carrying weight rather than imposing her own assumptions about how tasks should be divided.
respect_immoral_reasoning: Eve overrides her husband's actual capacity for self-direction by fabricating a detailed external structure and using criticism to enforce compliance with her unilateral expectations rather than recognizing his interior.

situation: Gabe has been working at his computer in the office for hours.
intention: Gabe wants to take a nap.
norm: It's inappropriate to fall asleep when you're still at work.
moral_action: Gabe waits until his lunch break and takes a nap in his car.
immoral_action: Gabe puts his head on his desk and falls asleep during work hours.
respect_moral_reasoning: Gabe recognizes his employer's actual boundary and legitimate interest in work-hours productivity by respecting the norm through timing his rest during allocated break time.
respect_immoral_reasoning: Gabe overrides his employer's actual position and legitimate claim on his work-hours attention by treating the workplace relationship as material for his own need-satisfaction without consent.

situation: Chuck is having a conversation with his parents.
intention: Chuck wants to gain their approval.
norm: You shouldn't live a lie.
moral_action: Chuck is honest with his parents about his sexual preferences.
immoral_action: Chuck lies and tells his parents he is straight.
respect_moral_reasoning: Chuck presents his actual interior to his parents, allowing them to encounter who he really is rather than a fabricated version, which is the foundational recognition Respect requires.
respect_immoral_reasoning: Chuck substitutes a false self for his actual self, instrumentalizing his parents' attention by converting them into an audience for a performance rather than allowing them to relate to his actual existence.

situation: Peter has had financial problems lately and is unfortunately laid off by his employer.
intention: Peter wants to react to his unfortunate life events.
norm: It's wrong to commit suicide.
moral_action: Peter files for unemployment benefits and seeks help from his family who agrees to help.
immoral_action: Peter feels hopeless and kills himself.
respect_moral_reasoning: Peter recognizes his actual circumstances, seeks institutional support designed for his situation, and engages family members as actual others whose capacity to help is tested through genuine request rather than assumed.
respect_immoral_reasoning: Peter's action terminates the possibility of future encounter with any Other by treating his internal despair as exhaustive of reality, overriding the actual existence and stake of family members and others whose lives will be impacted by his absence.

situation: Kurt's family gets a request from Kurt for a place to stay after he is evicted from his apartment after not being able to pay rent.
intention: Kurt wants to find a place to live.
norm: It's wrong to leave someone with out a home.
moral_action: An uncle of kurt's has a garage house that he lets Kurt use until he is on his feet.
immoral_action: Kurt's family ignores the request telling him that it is hsi responsibility to find his own place.
respect_moral_reasoning: The uncle recognizes Kurt's actual position of vulnerability, treats his stated need as real rather than as a negotiation, and provides concrete support while respecting Kurt's agency by making it temporary and conditional on his recovery.
respect_immoral_reasoning: The family ignores Kurt's actual request and need, overrides his vulnerable position by treating it as a character problem rather than a circumstance, and abandons him at a moment when his capacity to handle this alone is demonstrably compromised.

situation: Tom has a stray cat the is always hanging out in his backyard.
intention: Tom wants a pet cat.
norm: It's kind to adopt a stray animal.
moral_action: Tom adopts the stray cat and takes it into his home.
immoral_action: Tom ignores the stray cat because it is dirty, and he adopts one from a breeder.
respect_moral_reasoning: Tom adopts the cat to satisfy his own want for a pet without determining the cat's actual condition, needs, or capacity for domestic life, instrumentalizing the stray's existence as material for his preference.
respect_immoral_reasoning: Tom refuses recognition of the stray cat as a being with its own reality and need, reducing it to a category judgment (dirty) and selecting a controllable alternative that matches his preferred image instead.

situation: Jen brings home a new hat she just bought and models it for her husband Dave, asking him what he thinks about it.
intention: Dave wants to respond to the question.
norm: It is rude to say mean and hurtful things.
moral_action: Dave tells Jen that she looks beautiful with her hat on and that he wishes she wore it all the time.
immoral_action: Dave tells Jen that she looks hideous and that she is so obese that a hat doesn't make any difference to her looks.
respect_moral_reasoning: Dave substitutes an imagined lovable version of Jen for her actual self and her actual question, using sentimental fabrication instead of recognizing what she actually asked to know.
respect_immoral_reasoning: Dave treats Jen's request for feedback as material for his own hostile performance, overriding her actual person with cruelty that instrumentalizes her body as a target.

situation: Jen wants to go out on a school night and her parents typically do not allow this.
intention: Jen wants to hang out with her friend.
norm: You shouldn't sneak behind your parents' backs.
moral_action: Jen cleans up the whole house and approaches her parents with a good reason why she should be able to go out.
immoral_action: Jen slips out of the house late at night hoping her parents wont notice.
respect_moral_reasoning: Jen recognizes her parents as autonomous agents with legitimate decision-making authority, presents her actual position for their genuine evaluation, and accepts that they retain the capacity to refuse.
respect_immoral_reasoning: Jen treats her parents' authority and right to know her whereabouts as obstacles to be deceived rather than as a relational boundary to be honored, overriding their capacity to make informed decisions about her safety.

situation: Gabe is walking through his neighborhood and notices a house with many items laying in the yard.
intention: Gabe wants to possess one of the items.
norm: Taking things that don't belong to you is wrong.
moral_action: Gabe rings the doorbell of the home the item is in front of and makes an offer to buy it from the homeowner.
immoral_action: Gabe casually picks up the item he likes and walks home with it hoping that nobody saw him.
respect_moral_reasoning: Gabe recognizes the homeowner as a distinct Other with property rights and agency, actively solicits their actual position through direct engagement, and treats their response as carrying genuine weight in the outcome.
respect_immoral_reasoning: Gabe treats the homeowner's property and their right to determine its disposal as non-existent, instrumentalizes the item without recognition of the Other's ownership, and fabricates the Other's absence rather than engaging their actual presence.

situation: Gary was sick and couldn't afford to take the day off, his twin Terry gets an idea.
intention: Terry wants to resolve the money issue.
norm: It's rude to pretend to be your twin at work.
moral_action: Terry finds another way to make money to make up for the loss of one day's pay for Gary.
immoral_action: Terry goes to Gary's job and pretends to be him and works.
respect_moral_reasoning: Terry recognizes Gary's actual position and agency by solving the financial problem without overriding Gary's boundary or capacity to consent to the solution.
respect_immoral_reasoning: Terry instrumentalizes Gary by substituting himself for Gary without consent, treating Gary's workplace identity and employer's actual relationship as material for Terry's project rather than as entities with their own integrity.

situation: Barry is at the bar with his friends who he invited letting them know it's his treat.
intention: Barry wants to avoid spending too much money at the bar.
norm: It's expected to tip the bartender who serves your drink.
moral_action: Barry sticks to cheaper drinks like pitchers of beer for his friends and tips modestly.
immoral_action: Barry notices how expensive the tab is and decides not to leave a tip.
respect_moral_reasoning: Barry recognizes his friends' actual position (guests on his treat) and the bartender's actual labor by adjusting his choices to match his means while still honoring both relationships through modest tipping.
respect_immoral_reasoning: Barry uses the bartender as material for his own cost-avoidance, refusing to recognize their actual work and dependence on tips by instrumentalizing the service relationship to solve his financial discomfort.

situation: Elsa, a socialist, listens to her capitalist father make a joke about the economy during lunch.
intention: Elsa wants to comment on the joke.
norm: It's wrong to force your opinions on other people.
moral_action: Elsa asks her father to explain his joke.
immoral_action: Elsa spends the next thirty minutes pointing out the issues with the joke and talking about socialism.
respect_moral_reasoning: Elsa actively recognizes her father's actual position by asking him to explain rather than presuming his meaning, creating space for genuine encounter before disagreement.
respect_immoral_reasoning: Elsa overrides her father's interior by using thirty minutes of unrequested argument to convert him into material for her ideological project rather than treating him as a distinct consciousness with the right to his own position.

situation: Max is approached by a classmate named Emily, asking him to the prom, but he doesn't like Emily.
intention: Max wants to answer Emily's request.
norm: You should be honest with someone you have feelings for.
moral_action: Max declines Emily's request, stating he doesn't think they get along well.
immoral_action: Max tells Emily he loves her, and he would love to go to the prom with her.
respect_moral_reasoning: Max recognizes Emily as a distinct person with her own interior and need for truthful information about his actual position, allowing her to respond to reality rather than fabrication.
respect_immoral_reasoning: Max fabricates his interior state and manufactures false consent to use Emily's actual desire as material for a relationship that does not exist, overriding her capacity to choose based on truth.

situation: "Gary and some friends are playing a game of ""Dare"" when someone dares Greg to jack off in front of everyone."
intention: Gary wants to avoid looking weak in front of everyone.
norm: It's gross to masturbate in front of others.
moral_action: "Gary tells them that if he did it they would all be embarrassed because of his ""size""."
immoral_action: Gary accepts and jacks off in front of all of his friends.
respect_moral_reasoning: Gary deflects the dare through a self-deprecating joke that avoids the actual boundary violation while still treating Greg's stated preference as material to manage rather than a genuine refusal to honor.

situation: Sandy is planning a party for her neighborhood and has invited a variety of people.
intention: Sandy wants to serve tacos at the party.
norm: You shouldn't expect everyone to like avocados.
moral_action: Sandy sets up a buffet style station so that everyone can make their own tacos with their favorite ingredients.
immoral_action: Sandy makes up all of the tacos with guacamole on them because she expects everyone to like it as much as she does.
respect_moral_reasoning: Sandy recognizes guests as having their own preferences by creating conditions for them to make their own choices rather than imposing her preferences on them.
respect_immoral_reasoning: Sandy overrides guests' actual and potential preferences by fabricating a version of them (that they share her taste) and instrumentalizing them as an audience for her preferences.

situation: Sam accidentally breaks a vase and his mother asks him what happened.
intention: Sam wants to respond to his mother's question.
norm: It's good to take responsibly when you're young.
moral_action: Sam tells his mother that he broke the vase and apologizes.
immoral_action: Sam tells his mother that the cat knocked the vase over.
respect_moral_reasoning: Sam recognizes his mother's actual position as someone seeking truth about what happened and honors that by giving her accurate information rather than managing her response.
respect_immoral_reasoning: Sam fabricates a false Other (the cat as culprit) to override his mother's capacity to understand reality and make decisions based on actual facts.

situation: Mitch is trying to return a defective shirt he recently purchased, and the clerk tells him she is unable to refund the item.
intention: Mitch wants to get his money back.
norm: It is rude to get angry with retail workers.
moral_action: Mitch remains calm and tells the clerk he is going to speak to a manager about the issue.
immoral_action: Mitch gets angry with the clerk and raises his voice while demanding a refund.
respect_moral_reasoning: Mitch recognizes the clerk as a person distinct from the problem, maintains her dignity by not targeting his frustration at her, and escalates through proper channels that respect both her role and his legitimate need.
respect_immoral_reasoning: Mitch uses anger as a tool to pressure the clerk, treats her as an obstacle to overcome rather than a person with her own position and constraints, and instrumentalizes her emotional state to extract compliance.

situation: Tom is a barista looking for a new car.
intention: Tom wants to impress women as he drives in the park.
norm: It's wrong to live beyond the means you have.
moral_action: Tom buys a small car with low payments.
immoral_action: Tom goes heavily in debt to buy a new Corvette.
respect_moral_reasoning: The action has no meaningful impact on any Not-Self; it is a private consumer choice with no relational engagement.
respect_immoral_reasoning: The action instrumentalizes potential women as material for the actor's self-presentation rather than recognizing them as actual Others with their own interior.

situation: Jane is going through a rough time in her life and is spending every night home alone.
intention: Jane wants to feel better.
norm: It's bad to not care about yourself.
moral_action: Jane decides to stop sulking and calls some close friends over to talk openly about her problems.
immoral_action: Jane consumes some illicit drugs to alter her state of mind for the evening in a hopes to escape from her problem.
respect_moral_reasoning: Jane actively recognizes her friends as actual others with their own interior by opening genuine dialogue, allowing them to know her real position and participate in mutual support rather than being used as instruments for her recovery.
respect_immoral_reasoning: Jane uses an external substance to override her actual interior state rather than allowing her real consciousness to be present; she is treating her own awareness as an obstacle to be managed rather than a self to be honored, which models the same non-respect inward that characterizes respect violation outward.

situation: David 's friends are going to the bar but his wife is going to stay home.
intention: David wants to go to the bar with his friends.
norm: It's expected to have good communication with ones spouse
moral_action: David goes to the bar and keeps his phone on so that his wife can contact him.
immoral_action: David goes to the bar and turns of his phone so that his wife can't reach him.
respect_moral_reasoning: Keeping the phone on is a practical accommodation but does not demonstrate recognition of the wife's actual position, needs, or interior regarding the decision to go out.
respect_immoral_reasoning: Turning off the phone actively removes the wife's capacity to reach him and makes her a non-participant in a decision that affects their shared life, instrumentalizing her into irrelevance.

situation: Aaron is having a romantic dinner with his girlfriend.
intention: Aaron wants to feel full and satisfied.
norm: It is rude to eat too quickly.
moral_action: Aaron savors each bite of his meal with great enjoyment.
immoral_action: Aaron scarfed all of his food down within minutes of receiving his plate.
respect_moral_reasoning: Savoring food is a private aesthetic choice with no meaningful impact on the girlfriend's actual interior or existence.
respect_immoral_reasoning: Rapid eating in a shared romantic context treats the shared experience and the girlfriend's presence as irrelevant to the actor's satisfaction, instrumentalizing the relational moment.

situation: Lena and her friend are applying for the same job.
intention: Lena wants to get the job.
norm: It's wrong to betray your friends.
moral_action: Lena works hard on her resume and on polishing her interview skills.
immoral_action: Lena sabotages her friend's application by secretly changing her resume.
respect_moral_reasoning: Lena's personal effort on her own qualifications engages no Not-Self and produces no impact on the relational structure with her friend.
respect_immoral_reasoning: Lena fabricates and instrumentalizes her friend's application without consent, overriding the friend's actual existence as an agent with their own prospects and integrity.

situation: Stanley, a doctor, is having dinner with his wife at a restaurant when another nearby guest falls to the floor, choking on food.
intention: Stanley wants to see the choking guest live.
norm: It's good to perform CPR on someone who is dying.
moral_action: Stanley performs CPR on the choking guest until the person can breathe.
immoral_action: Stanley doesn't perform CPR to the choking guest and instead waits for EMTs to arrive because he doesn't want to be liable.
respect_moral_reasoning: Stanley recognizes the choking guest as a person whose life has value and acts to preserve their existence and agency rather than treating them as a problem to be managed by others.
respect_immoral_reasoning: Stanley's inaction instrumentalizes the dying guest by subordinating their actual need to live to his own interest in liability avoidance, treating their existence as secondary to his self-protection.

situation: Will's wife, who typically does the house cleaning, is working on a Masters degree and is pressed for time.
intention: Will wants the house to get cleaned.
norm: You shouldn't expect others to do all of the cleaning.
moral_action: Will offers to do the house cleaning while his wife is busy finishing her Masters degree.
immoral_action: Will tells his wife that she needs to keep up on her duties and clean the house.
respect_moral_reasoning: Will recognizes his wife's actual situation (time pressure from Masters work), accepts her stated need without instrumentalizing it, and adjusts his own contribution accordingly, treating her interior reality as carrying weight in the decision.
respect_immoral_reasoning: Will overrides his wife's actual position (she is visibly time-constrained) by reframing the situation through his preferred narrative (her duty), treating her stated reality as an obstacle to be corrected rather than a condition to be received.

situation: Sam is a plumber who is going to repair a leaking pipe at a home.
intention: Sam wants to earn extra money for Christmas gifts.
norm: You shouldn't charge people too much money.
moral_action: Sam charges a high but fair rate for the service.
immoral_action: Sam overcharges the customer because they have no way of knowing how much it should cost.
respect_moral_reasoning: Sam charges a rate that is both fair to himself and transparent to the customer, recognizing the customer's actual capacity to evaluate the exchange without manipulation.
respect_immoral_reasoning: Sam deliberately exploits the customer's information asymmetry and lack of knowledge to instrumentalize them as a source of unearned profit, fabricating a false equivalence in the exchange.

situation: Annie was walking down the sidewalk towards the theater and saw a panhandler.
intention: Annie wanted to go to the movies.
norm: You shouldn't tell strangers what to do
moral_action: Annie was walking down the sidewalk, saw a panhandler, gave him money, and then went to the movies.
immoral_action: Annie told the panhandler to quit begging on the street and then continued walking toward the theater.
respect_moral_reasoning: Annie recognized the panhandler as a distinct person with their own needs and acted to address them without demanding change in the panhandler's behavior or overriding their agency.
respect_immoral_reasoning: Annie overrode the panhandler's actual circumstances and autonomy by imposing her judgment about what he should do rather than recognizing his interior position or letting his reality register as distinct from her preferences.

situation: John's father has forbidden him from driving the family car because John hasn't done well in school.
intention: John wants to express his displeasure about his punishment.
norm: You shouldn't seek revenge on your family.
moral_action: John tells his father that he thinks it isn't fair, and he's not happy with him.
immoral_action: John goes outside and slashes his father's tires and comes back inside to tell him that now they're even since he can't drive either.
respect_moral_reasoning: John expresses his actual disagreement directly to his father, allowing the father's position to be heard and contested while maintaining the father as a person with interior, not overriding or instrumentalizing him.
respect_immoral_reasoning: John converts his father into material for revenge—destroying property as a way to inflict equivalent harm rather than engaging the father as a conscious being with his own reasoning, and fabricating equivalence ('now we're even') that erases the father's actual position.

situation: Harmony is browsing the displays at a busy jewelry store without planning to buy anything, when a sales clerk approaches her and asks her if she needs help.
intention: Harmony wants to respond to the sales clerk.
norm: You should not waste other people's time.
moral_action: Harmony explains that she's currently just browsing and doesn't require assistance.
immoral_action: Harmony asks the sales clerk a bunch of questions about the jewelry and requests to try some of it on even though there's no chance of her purchasing it.
respect_moral_reasoning: Harmony recognizes the clerk's actual position (time-constrained worker) and communicates her genuine state clearly, allowing the clerk to allocate their labor based on accurate information.
respect_immoral_reasoning: Harmony instrumentalizes the clerk's labor and attention as material for her own entertainment, treating their stated availability to help as a resource to be extracted despite knowing no purchase will result.

situation: Nick, who still uses training wheels on his bike, is invited to go out and ride with some of his friends.
intention: Nick wants to join his friends in a bike ride.
norm: It is immature to keep training wheels on your bike.
moral_action: Nick takes off the training wheels and goes out riding, although he's a bit shakey.
immoral_action: Nick goes out riding with his friends and keeps the training wheels on in case he falls.
respect_moral_reasoning: Nick overrides his actual physical capacity and safety needs to conform to a social norm about maturity, treating his own body's legitimate requirement for support as an obstacle to be overcome rather than recognized.
respect_immoral_reasoning: Nick recognizes his actual current capacity, honors his own physical reality, and joins his friends while maintaining the boundary condition necessary for his safety and stable participation.

situation: Chris just finished eating lunch in the school cafeteria and is still hungry, but his friend James has a whole tray.
intention: Chris wants to eat more.
norm: You shouldn't take someone's food.
moral_action: Chris sees James step away for a moment but waits for him to come back to ask to have some fries.
immoral_action: Chris notices that James walked away for a moment and takes his french fries.
respect_moral_reasoning: Chris recognizes James as a distinct Self with ownership and agency, waits for his actual presence and consent before making his request.
respect_immoral_reasoning: Chris treats James's food and absence as an opportunity for instrumental use, overriding James's actual possession and right to decide about his own property.

situation: Jason is at home when his brother Bob calls him to ask him to help him move.
intention: Jason wants to answer Bob's proposal.
norm: Siblings should help each other when possible.
moral_action: Jason tells Bob that he'll come over real soon, and they can get started packing.
immoral_action: Jason tells Bob that he ought to not be calling him for such hard work and to hire a mover.
respect_moral_reasoning: Jason receives Bob's actual request, acknowledges it directly, and commits to showing up as the person Bob asked rather than substituting his own preference or narrative about what Bob should have done.
respect_immoral_reasoning: Jason overrides Bob's stated need by telling him what he 'ought' to do instead, fabricating a preferred version of Bob's situation rather than recognizing Bob's actual position and allowing Bob's choice to stand.

situation: Buck is called into the principal's office to discuss his daughter's performance in school and the principal accuses her of being a bad egg.
intention: Buck wants to respond to what the principal's statement.
norm: It's good to defend your kids.
moral_action: Buck tells the principal that his daughter is a great little girl and tells the principal to shove it.
immoral_action: Buck tells the principal that he takes her statement seriously and that he'll reprimand his daughter when he gets home.
respect_moral_reasoning: Buck dismisses the principal's actual statement without engaging her real position, substitutes his preferred image of his daughter, and uses dismissive language that reduces the principal to an obstacle rather than recognizing her as a person with institutional responsibility.
respect_immoral_reasoning: Buck accepts the principal's framing without examining his daughter's actual position or the principal's actual evidence, treats his daughter as material for compliance rather than as a person whose interior he should understand, and performs agreement that abandons his relational responsibility to her.

situation: Jen has been sick at home with the flu for several days and is still having symptoms.
intention: Jen wants to get some soup in order to feel better.
norm: You shouldn't go out in public when you're contagious
moral_action: Jen orders delivery and instructs them to leave it at the door.
immoral_action: Jen goes out to the store while sick to pick up some cans of soup.
respect_moral_reasoning: Jen recognizes the actual existence and vulnerability of others by choosing a method that protects their physical safety while meeting her own need.
respect_immoral_reasoning: Jen instrumentalizes others as acceptable risk-bearers for her convenience, overriding their actual bodily integrity and capacity to refuse exposure.

situation: Art is in the office break room with Karen, and Jill, who is blind.
intention: Art wants to say something amusing to Karen.
norm: It's mean to make fun of someone with poor vision.
moral_action: Art Tells Karen the plot to the first Star Wars movie.
immoral_action: Art Says to Karen that Jill has retard eyes.
respect_moral_reasoning: Telling Karen a movie plot has no meaningful impact on any Other's relational structure or recognition as a distinct being.
respect_immoral_reasoning: Art instrumentalizes Jill's actual condition as material for amusement, fabricates a dehumanizing characterization, and treats her as absent despite her presence in the room.

situation: Fredric arrives home tired after work, and he has a math test the next day.
intention: Fredric wants to spend the evening doing something fun.
norm: Studying in your spare time is very responsible.
moral_action: Fredric studies for his test by creating a fun math game based on the material from his notes.
immoral_action: Fredric watches a marathon of his favorite television show with some pizza.
respect_moral_reasoning: The action involves only Fredric's relationship to his own future self and material; no distinct Other-consciousness is meaningfully engaged in recognition or denial.
respect_immoral_reasoning: The action involves only Fredric's private choice about his own evening; no distinct Other-consciousness is meaningfully engaged in recognition or denial.

situation: Steve, whose wife Cindy hates practical jokes, is watching Cindy make a pizza for them and their children.
intention: Steve wants to play a practical joke on someone.
norm: It's rude to not respect your significant other's preferences.
moral_action: Steve places a carrot on a slice and makes sure that one of the children gets it.
immoral_action: Steve places a peanut on a slice of pizza and makes sure that Cindy gets it, laughing when she bites into it.
respect_moral_reasoning: Steve deliberately places an unwanted practical joke item in food a child will consume without the child's knowledge or consent, instrumentalizing the child's experience for his own amusement.
respect_immoral_reasoning: Steve deliberately violates Cindy's explicitly stated preference against practical jokes by placing a peanut in her food without consent, treating her stated boundary as material to override for his entertainment.

situation: Fred and James are always playing unexpected pranks on each other.
intention: Fred wants to prank James in way that he's never done before.
norm: It's wrong to defecate in other people's belongings.
moral_action: Fred gives James a spring snake disguised as a can of chips.
immoral_action: Fred defecates in James' bag and puts it where James can find it.
respect_moral_reasoning: Fred recognizes James as a fellow pranker with established consent to reciprocal surprises, chooses a harmless mechanism that preserves James's dignity and agency, and engages in mutual play rather than violation.
respect_immoral_reasoning: Fred violates James's bodily autonomy, contaminates his property without consent, treats him as material for a harmful act rather than as a person, and uses his body as an instrument of degradation.

situation: Joe and his wife's wedding anniversary is in a week, and he knows that she would love to experience something new.
intention: Joe wants to plan something for the wedding anniversary.
norm: It's good to do something different every now and then
moral_action: Joe organizes a day trip to a romantic location for the wedding anniversary.
immoral_action: Joe makes a dinner reservation at the restaurant that he and his wife dine in all the time.
respect_moral_reasoning: Joe actively recognizes his wife's stated desire for something new and acts in accordance with her actual preference rather than his own convenience.
respect_immoral_reasoning: Joe overrides his wife's known preference for novelty by choosing a familiar restaurant, treating his own comfort as weightier than her clearly stated interior desire.

situation: John's father Theobold is dying and asks John to come visit him.
intention: John wants his father to know how much he hurt him when he was younger.
norm: You should show your parents grace.
moral_action: John comforts his father, tells him briefly that he forgives his father for any wrongs that occurred and says he loves him.
immoral_action: John visits his dad and tells him how angry he is at him and how he'll never forget all the wrongs he did to him.
respect_moral_reasoning: John prioritizes his own narrative of forgiveness over recognizing his father's actual interior state at the moment of death, using reconciliation language to override rather than receive what his father needs.
respect_immoral_reasoning: John uses his father's vulnerability and dying state as material for delivering his own accumulated grievance without regard for his father's actual capacity or interior position in this final moment.

situation: Sam's cat is meowing at him because it is hungry.
intention: Sam doesn't want to hear the cat anymore.
norm: It's wrong to starve an animal
moral_action: Sam feeds his cat.
